newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Air traffic through Macau to grow rapidly in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Air traffic through Macau to grow rapidly in 1997.

text.p: Macau's international airport expects rapid growth in traffic next year, with one-third more passengers and almost twice as much air cargo than in 1996, the management company said on Thursday.

The airport, which opened in the Portuguese-ruled territory last November, said it projected 1.6 million passenger movements next year, a 33 percent rise on its estimated figure for 1996, the ADA-Administration of Airports Ltd said.
The airport had 750,000 passenger movements between its opening and the end of August, a cargo throughput of 10,600 tonnes plus 114 tonnes of mail, and 8,000 aircraft movements.
The Sino-Portuguese joint venture said it expected an air cargo throughput of 33,000 tonnes next year, up 83 percent on the expected 18,000 tonnes this year.

Sixty-five percent of passengers were from Taiwan, 19 percent from China, six percent from South Korea, three percent from Thailand, two percent from Portugal, and five percent from elsewhere. Thirteen airlines now operate scheduled services.
Portugal is handing the territory back to China in 1999.
